params.name: run_as
params.description: The executing user of the action. If not provided, the action will be run on behalf of the user/machine who initiated the action (identified by the bearer token used to execute this route).

params.name: action_identifier
params.description: The identifier of the action/automation you want to operate on.

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

This route allows you to fetch the details of an action run.

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

:::info Version parameter
Set the `version` parameter to `v2` for the latest version of the API.
:::

items.docs:
This route allows you to update an action run's details. This can be used to update the run's status & label, and add links to it (e.g. external logs of the job runner).

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

items.docs:
This route allows you to approve or decline a request to execute an action that requires approval.

To learn more about manual approval for actions, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/set-self-service-actions-rbac/#configure-manual-approval-for-actions).

:::info Version parameter value
Set the `version` parameter to `v2` for the latest version of the API.
:::

params.description: The identifier of the blueprint associated with the action run.

params.name: active
params.description: If `true`, only running action runs will be fetched.

params.description: The email of the user who initiated the action run.

params.name: user_id
params.description: The id of the user who initiated the action run.

params.description: The maximum number of action runs to fetch.

params.description: The fields to exclude from the response

params.name: external_run_id
params.description: The run id of your backend, for example the id that GitHub gives the workflow. This can be used to identify the action run instead of the `run_id`.

items.docs:
This route allows you to fetch all action runs in your Port account. The route will perform a logical `AND` between all query parameters below, and return all action runs that match the criteria.

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

:::info Version parameter
Set the `version` parameter to `v2` for the latest version of the API.
:::

params.name: limit
params.description: The maximum number of logs to fetch.

params.name: offset
params.description: The number of logs to skip.

params.name: run_id
params.description: The identifier of the action run.

items.docs:
This route allows you to fetch the logs from an action run.

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

info.name: Add a log to an action run

params.name: run_id
params.description: The identifier of the action run.

items.docs:
This route allows you to send a log message back to Port, which will be displayed in the action run's page. You can also use this route to update the run's termination status (SUCCESS/FAILURE) and label describing the status.

To learn more about action runs, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/reflect-action-progress/).

params.name: include_pending_approvers
params.description: If `true`, the route will also return the users who have not yet approved the action run.

params.name: run_id
params.description: The identifier of the action run.

items.docs:
This route allows you to fetch the approvers of a specific action run.

To learn more about manual approval for actions, check out the [documentation](https://docs.port.io/create-self-service-experiences/set-self-service-actions-rbac/#configure-manual-approval-for-actions).
